reasons: Anchors opened: Lith. prašyti and maldyti (asyndetic, entreating the father; second anchor 1sg. cond. Prašyčiau, maldyčiau) and ORu Suzdal chronicle молити (reflexive) with просити (+ gen. мира). Both pairs are exact cognates and morphologically parallel o-grade iteratives (prašyti = prositi; maldyti = *modliti/moliti < *moldʰ-, Derksen), so the formal match is good. But a binomial of the two ordinary verbs of entreaty is near-generic, the ORu has reflexive молитися and a different construction (просити + gen. 'ask for peace'), the order differs, OCS gospel usage (Mk 11:24) provides a Church model, and Lithuanian dainos are exposed to Slavic (Belarusian/Polish) prosić/molić. Contact cannot be excluded.

reasons: Anchors opened: Lith. prijojo with žalia, gire (OCR for acc. žalią girę) and Vuk 28247:33 језди with кроз + гору, зелену. Three cognate slots hold: joti ~ jezditi (*(H)yeh2-, Slavic -zd- derivative), giria ~ gora (*gʷorH-; Derksen notes SCr. gora 'wood' dial. and Lith. 'woods' < 'wooded mountain'), žalias ~ zelen (*ǵʰelH-, different suffixes). Interesting shared 'forest' sense of the mountain noun. But 'ride through the green forest' is a stock ballad scene in every European tradition, the epithet is generic, and Baltic–Slavic contact is intense; the cognate choice follows from these being the basic words. Defensible Balto-Slavic stock phrase, not compelling inheritance.
known: žalia giria ~ zelena gora parallels are noted in Balto-Slavic folk-poetics; uncertain.

reasons: Anchors opened. Lith. 1 (Leskien 11316): he did not take (neėmė) her offered white hand (baltos rankos, gen. of negation) — hand as object. Lith. 2 (33194): nuimsi + ant + baltų rankelių 'take off onto/at the white hands' — hand is a location, not taken; does not support. Serbian Vuk 33314:39: узима + је + за + бијелу руку 'takes her by the white hand' — the girl is object, hand is the grip point (za + acc.): syntax not congruent. Cognates acceptable (imti ~ -imati *h1em-; ranka ~ ruka; baltas ~ bijel only root-related, different formations). 'White hand' is a pan-European folk epithet and taking by the hand a universal gesture.

Anchors opened: Rybnikov wedding song (bride given 'to a foreign side' lists свекоръ, свекруха, деверья, then золовушки; each in-law then mocks her, 28067-28073) and Helen's lament Il. 24.768-770 (δαέρων, γαλόων, εἰνατέρων, ἑκυρή, ἑκυρός who reproached her). Cognates are all secure (свекор/ἑκυρός *swéḱuros; свекры/ἑκυρά *sweḱrúh2 — свекруха is a Russian suffixal renewal; деверь/δαήρ; золовка/γάλως), and the theme (incoming wife reproached by husband's kin) is strikingly congruent. But the inherited element is the kinship lexicon itself; listing these terms whenever a bride's in-laws are discussed is semantically induced, and the 'reproach by in-laws' theme is common to patrilocal lament traditions everywhere. Strong lexical-cultural continuity, weak as phraseology.
known: Yes for the lexical set: the PIE husband's-kin terms (and RV 10.85.46, Il. 24.769) are standard handbook evidence for patrilocality (Delbrück, Benveniste, Mallory-Adams).

reasons: Anchors opened. Lith. Leskien 12913: imperatives 'set (leiskis), sun; rise (tekėk), moon' — tekėti here is 'rise', applied only to the moon. reasons: Anchors opened: Agathangelos 1365 (Gregory 'does not wish to live (keal) and see the light (zloys, tesanel)'), AVŚ 12.2.36 (jyok, sūryaṃ, dṛśe), Lucretius 3.849 (lumina, uitae). The figure 'see the light (of the sun)' = live is real (Il. 18.61, Vedic jyók with sū́ryaṃ, dṛśé) and Armenian has it outside Christian text (Movses' Artawazd curse, support). But the cognate pairs are scattered across different anchors: Arm. loys ~ Lat. lūmen (*lewk-) where Latin has no 'see' and means 'light of life'; Arm. tesanem ~ Ved. dṛś only if *derḱ- with r-loss is accepted (Martirosyan §2.1.33.3, 'material scanty'), and the objects differ (light vs sun). Biblical 'see light' (Job 3:16, Ps 49:19) and the Greek Vorlage tradition of Agathangelos are plausible models for the Armenian line.
